title: Learning
content: Learning is something you never stop doing. No matter how old you are. Sometimes it's not very obvious you are learning, because you are not actively pursing a certain subject, but trust me, you are always learning. Before becoming a stay-at-home mom I spent my late teens learning about business and concentrated on accounting. I worked a couple different jobs with different accounting roles, but then decided it was time for me to take on a new adventure, one that I had dreamed of since childhood, becoming a parent. Now that my kids are older though, it's time for me to start contributing my skills to society by getting back out in the workforce. I decided I really didn't like accounting as much as I thought I did when I was younger, so I started pursuing the field of technology. I started by trying to teach myself how to code with Python, which is a pretty robust and popular programming language. Not having an experience in this at all made it very difficult to really learn how to program, I didn't really have anyone with a lot of experience and knowledge in Python to ask questions to when I got stuck, so I kind of stepped away from that for a little bit and focused all my energy on my babies. After my kids started becoming more independent and keeping themselves entertained, I looked into courses that taught Python. I found a Data Analytics Boot Camp and completed the boot camp, which helped me take a big leap into really understanding and utilizing Python. After that  boot camp, not necessarily liking a big subject matter inherent in Data Analytics(statistics) I decided to find free self-study to further build my skills with Python. I really enjoyed Python, but didn't really know how to translate my knowledge into a career, at the time when I was looking, there were a lot of developer roles that required experience with C#, which I had some, but really did not like the syntax and rules needed in that language. Anyway, I started thinking about what I would like to do, and fell into web development. Currently I'm doing an online self-study boot camp through Udemy for Full Stack Development. I really hope I am able to build my skills to the point where I can finally break into the field of technology! So there you go, you are always learning, whether it's an active pursuit, like my self-study, or learning that just happens through new experiences, like parenthood!
